title: Make consolidated-report degrade gracefully when an upstream tier's artifact is missing
summary: When Tier 3 times out before uploading benchmark-scale-report, the consolidated-report job's unconditional artifact download fails outright, turning one real upstream failure into two failure entries in the run summary.
description:
In the observed run (https://github.com/priyanshu-krishnan1/yaadien/actions/runs/31242532940), Tier 3 was cancelled on timeout before its "Upload benchmark scale report artifact" step ran, so no `benchmark-scale-report` artifact ever existed. The downstream `consolidated-report` job (`.github/workflows/benchmark-suite.yml`, step "Download locust-scale-report (BM-14 + BM-15)" area, ~line 989 onward) then failed with: `Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name: benchmark-scale-report`. The job otherwise completed successfully (per the run summary, `Consolidated benchmark report` shows as passing overall — the specific download step is what errored, per the annotations list) and still produced the Job Summary and gh-pages output for everything else.

This is minor relative to CIF-1/2/3/4/5 (the actual root causes), but it doubles the apparent failure surface for anyone triaging a run: a single Tier 3 timeout currently reads as two separate red X's, making the real problem slightly harder to spot at a glance in the Actions UI.

Fix: wrap the `benchmark-scale-report` (and any other tier-specific) artifact download in `if: always()` plus `continue-on-error: true`, or check artifact existence first (`actions/download-artifact` supports this, or use the GitHub API to list artifacts before attempting the download), and have the report-generation step note "Tier 3 did not complete / no scale report available this run" in the Job Summary and gh-pages output instead of hard-failing the step. Apply the same treatment to any other per-tier artifact download in this job that has the same unconditional-download pattern.

Acceptance: re-run (or simulate) a scenario where Tier 3 fails/times out before uploading its artifact, and confirm `consolidated-report` completes cleanly, clearly notes the missing tier's data in its summary, and does not itself show as a failed step.
